title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a continuation of the 'équation des lacets' from La Longue Marche, now treated relatively. Over a base scheme S one has a form G of GL(2)_S. It carries sections ρ and σ, the analogues of the modular generators ρ = (0 1; -1 1), of order 6, and σ = (0 -1; 1 0), of order 4, in SL2(Z). One considers conjugates ξ = α ρ α^{-1} and η = β σ β^{-1}. The loop equation asks that ξ and η differ by a unipotent 'loop' element ℓ_1^ν, written ε_1(μ-1) in the present notation, i.e. an element of a Borel-unipotent one-parameter subgroup 1 + λN.

On the previous page Grothendieck derived explicit formulas in the modular case: a = (cρ+d)/(c²+cd+d²) and b = (tσ+u)/(t²+u²). He then hit a discrepancy with the factor τ_∞^2 (involving a class α_2(μ) ∈ Z/2) from the earlier 'brutal' computations (p. 398', (78)).

On this page he resolves the apparent incompatibility. In the earlier text (loc. cit.) the loop equation was written with a possible sign, ξ = ε η ℓ_1^ν with ε ∈ {±1}. The present 'simpler' theory tacitly assumes ε = +1, so the older equation is a generalization of the present one.

He therefore proposes to redo the theory for the general equation (96) ξ = ε·η·ε_1(μ-1), with ε a central section of G. Taking determinants of both sides gives det ε = 1: indeed det ρ = det σ = 1 and the unipotent factor has determinant 1. For a scalar ε this means ε² = 1, i.e. ε ∈ μ_2(S). He remarks there is no reason to assume ε ∈ {±1}: over a non-connected base, or in characteristic 2, μ_2(S) is larger. He decides to continue first with ε = +1.

The sign is the familiar lift ambiguity between PSL2 and SL2: -1 = σ² = ρ³ lies in the kernel, so relations valid in PSL2(Z) or the profinite/Galois setting lift to SL2 only up to ±1. This is plausibly the origin of the τ_∞^2 factor.
errors: No real error. Note that 'ε section de G' must mean a central (scalar) section for det ε = ε² to hold; for a general section, det ε = 1 does not give ε² = 1. Grothendieck presumably means a section of the centre G_m.
Equation number: (95) was already used on the previous page; the label here appears to be overwritten as (96).

ideas.what: Loop equation with a central sign: ξ = ε η ℓ_1^ν, with ε² = 1 forced by determinants and ε a section of μ_2(S) rather than ±1
ideas.modern_name: Central (μ_2) ambiguity in lifting relations from PSL2 to SL2 / GL2; the ±1 kernel of SL2(Z) → PSL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; the loop equation itself is Grothendieck's (La Longue Marche, 1981)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated 1981; edited by J. Malgoire) contains the 'équation des lacets' with sign; this relative-scheme version is unpublished

ideas.what: Relative treatment of the modular loop equation over a base scheme S for forms of GL(2)_S
ideas.modern_name: Torsors and forms of GL2 / Azumaya algebras of rank 4; relative moduli of triangle/modular structures
ideas.where_published: Framework in SGA3; the specific application is in these unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes

deep.surprise_reason: A bookkeeping page: Grothendieck notices that the earlier version of the loop equation carried a sign ε = ±1, which explains the τ_∞^2 discrepancy. He notes that ε should be a section of μ_2 and postpones the general case. The content is routine and has no independent significance beyond the internal development of the notes.
transcription_corrections: '! premier vu' should read 'À première vue'.
'c'est donc une généralisation par à l'équation pour ce disant' should read approximately 'c'est donc une généralisation par rapport à l'équation présente, où on suppose ε=+1'.
'ε_1(β1-1)' should read 'ε_1(μ-1)' (or ℓ_1(μ-1)), i.e. ℓ_1^ν in the current notation.
The equation label appears to be (96), overwritten, not (95).
'(en prenant les dét. des deux membres) ... ε² = 1': the struck-out fragment preceding ε is illegible.
